FELIX FINSTER, NIELS G. GRESNIGT, JOS´E M. ISIDRO, ANTONINO MARCIAN`O,

Abstract. We compare the structures and methods in the theory of causal fermion
systems with approaches to fundamental physics based on division algebras, in par-
ticular the octonions. We find that octonions and, more generally, tensor products

configuration of a causal fermion system. This is achieved by associating the real

blocks.title: Introduction
blocks.content: []{#secintro label="secintro"} This article is part of a series of papers comparing the structures and ideas of different approaches to fundamental physics that was started with [@eth-cfs; @mmt-cfs] and will be continued in [@cfstdqg; @tracedynamics]. Each of these papers contains an introduction to the theories under consideration including an overview of their accomplishments. These overviews serve as a starting point for a reader familiar with one of the approaches to engage with the other approach. The papers proceed with a detailed comparison of these two theories. blocks.title: Division Algebras and the Standard Model
Motivation
blocks.content:
The standard model of particle physics is a gauge theory based on the group ${\rm{SU}}(3)\times {\rm{SU}}(2)\times {\rm{U}}(1)$ with particle multiplets falling into irreducible representations of these Lie groups. Despite its undeniable success, the standard model has some striking theoretical and conceptual puzzles that remain unanswered. For example:

-   What is the origin of the standard model gauge group, and why do the gauge groups, as well as the spacetime symmetries appear as separate factors?

blocks.title: Historical Overview
The Normed Division Algebras
blocks.content: A division algebra is an algebra over a field where division is always well-defined, except by zero. A normed division algebra has the additional property that it is also a normed vector space, with the norm defined in terms of a conjugate. A well-known result by Hurwitz [@hurwitz1898ueber] states that there exist only four normed division algebras (over the field of real numbers): $\mathbb{R}$, $\mathbb{C}$, $\mathbb{H}$, $\mathbb{O}$, being of dimensions one, two, four and eight, respectively. Causal Fermion Systems
blocks.content: []{#seccfsintro label="seccfsintro"} We now give a self-contained introduction to the basic structures of a causal fermion system. We keep the explanations short, noting that detailed and elementary introductions to the physical and mathematical concepts can be found in the review papers [@dice2014; @review] and the comparison paper [@mmt-cfs Section 2.1]. We also refer the interested reader to the textbooks [@cfs; @intro] and the website [@cfsweblink].

blocks.title: Spacetime Structures
blocks.content:
A causal fermion system describes a spacetime together with all structures therein. The structures are the causal and metric structures, spinors and interacting fields (for details see [@cfs Chapter 1]). All these spacetime structures are *inherent* in the sense that they use information already encoded in the causal fermion system. We now give a brief outline of the spacetime structures, with a focus on those structures which will be needed later on.

blocks.title: Comparison
blocks.content: []{#sec:comparison label="sec:comparison"} In this section we will highlight and compare the mathematical structures and the conceptional ideas behind causal fermion systems and octonionic approaches to fundamental physics, and we will demonstrate a first simple example of how octonions can be integrated in causal fermion systems.

blocks.title: Foundations of the Approaches
blocks.content:
[]{#sec:foundations label="sec:foundations"} We begin with a discussion of the basic ideas and the mathematical structures of the theories.

### Octonionic Approaches

Octonionic (division algebraic) approaches to the standard model remain an active research program, with different approaches considered in the literature. The underlying goal of these approaches is to find the correct algebraic structures, often in the form of tensor products of the division algebras, from which the gauge groups and particle content of the standard model may be derived, as well as the Lorentz group for the grav

blocks.title: Connection to the Gauge Group of the Standard Model
blocks.content:
[]{#sec:gaugegroup label="sec:gaugegroup"} Obtaining the gauge group of the standard model is a key objective for any fundamental physical theory. Here we summarize the current status of this quest in both approaches and discuss what we can learn from a comparison.

### Octonionic Approaches

Algebraic approaches based on the octonions (or more generally the division algebras) attempt to recover the standard model gauge groups as those groups that preserve certain subspaces of the underlying algebraic structure. blocks.title: Describing the Three Generations in the Standard Model
blocks.content:
[]{#secthreegen label="secthreegen"} We now explain and compare how the three generations of elementary particles (like $e$, $\mu$ and $\tau$) come up in the different approaches.

### Octonionic Approaches

Although existing division algebraic approaches provide an elegant construction of the internal space of a single generation of leptons and quarks, a comprehensive algebraic explanation for the existence of three generations remains to be found[^1].

blocks.content: []{#secoutlook label="secoutlook"} In this section, we given an outlook and explain directions of future research.

blocks.title: Connection with the Exceptional Lie Groups and Jordan Algebras
blocks.content: []{#sece68 label="sece68"} In Section [\[secthreegen\]](#secthreegen){reference-type="ref" reference="secthreegen"} we saw that describing the interactions of the standard model in the setting of causal fermion systems naturally leads to the exceptional Jordan algebra. Moreover, it brings with it the exceptional Lie groups which have a direct connection with the octonions. We now outline these connections, also pointing towards directions of future research.
